source_quotes.condition_other: The participant in question had a belowknee amputation in March of 2003 due to posttraumatic arthritis, then a surgical revision in February of 2016 using TMR to address three painful neuromas in his residual limb, one for each of the peroneal, tibial and sural nerves.
source_quotes.blinding: We verified these self-reports through palpation of muscle during voluntary movement by the patient and our formal, single-blinded cutaneous stimulation of the residual limb.
source_quotes.exposures[0].target.label: iFU stimulation of his non-functioning tibial nerve under ultrasound image guidance (Fig. 1b) with sufficient spatial peak temporal average intensity (71.5 W/cm<sup>2</sup>, 2.0 MHz, for each of five individual pulses of 0.1 second in duration, spaced 1e2 seconds apart) produced corresponding transient pulses of phantom limb sensations, the first time the participant had felt sensations of any sort associated with his tibial nerve since his TMR surgery.

source_quotes.n_subjects: During a study to determine the relative sensitivity to external stimulation of transected nerves after standard amputation versus TMR, we encountered a single participant who recovered motor and sensory function of their tibial nerve after TMR surgery during ultrasound stimulation of the nerve.
source_quotes.n_sessions_per_subject: Up to and including the time the participant left our facility, he reported voluntary control of and sensations associated with his lateral gastrocnemius muscle.

flags.reason: Paper labels this value 'spatial peak temporal average intensity' (which matches the schema's ispta_w_cm2 field name), but it is placed in isppa_w_cm2 because it is delivered as five discrete 0.1 s pulses rather than a continuous exposure long enough for a temporal-average interpretation to be unambiguous; flagged for reviewer judgement. No domain (free-field vs in-situ) is stated, so placed in unspecified_domain.

The 2.0 MHz frequency is stated explicitly only for the tibial nerve stimulation; the peroneal nerve stimulation used 'a comparable intensity value' with the same device in the same session, and frequency was not independently restated for it.
No vocabulary term covers post-amputation/TMR peripheral nerve injury; classified as other with condition_other text.

condition_other: Below-knee amputee with targeted muscle reinnervation (TMR) and non-functioning tibial nerve (peripheral nerve injury / neuroma after amputation)
readout_other: Clinical observation and participant report of voluntary/involuntary muscle movement and cutaneous sensation; real-time diagnostic ultrasound imaging used to guide stimulation and to directly observe muscle movement
direction_notes: iFU stimulation of the non-functioning tibial nerve produced phantom limb sensations and, at a second intensity, involuntary followed by voluntary movement of the lateral gastrocnemius muscle and recovered cutaneous sensation, restoring motor and sensory function that had been absent since TMR surgery.

exposures.label: iFU stimulation of the tibial nerve

target.label: non-functioning tibial nerve (distal transected nerve after TMR)

timing.protocol_description: Five individual 0.1-second iFU pulses were delivered per intensity value, spaced 1-2 seconds apart, using a ramp-up paradigm starting at low intensity and increasing until a first discernible sensation was achieved; after an initial 71.5 W/cm2 exposure, stimulation continued at a lower intensity (66.5 W/cm2) within 1 minute.

exposures.label: iFU stimulation of the peroneal nerve

timing.protocol_description: During the same session, the transected peroneal nerve was successfully stimulated at a comparable intensity value (66.5 W/cm2) as used for the tibial nerve.
